decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Tauros for immediate Prankster Tailwind, Intimidate, and Rock Slide pressure against Charizard/Venusaur while retaining a strong Excadrill answer. Ninetales can reset sun on a later switch, and Gholdengo gives reliable spread damage and a Poison-immunity option.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s confirmed sun mode centers on Charizard-Y and Venusaur; Excadrill is a Focus Sash Mold Breaker follow-up with Rapid Spin, Earthquake, and a Speed boost, while Rotom-Wash supports it. Preserve weather disruption and maintain a dedicated Excadrill answer. Mega Blastoise is vulnerable to the sun combination and should not be an automatic selection. Gholdengo and Maushold are useful alternatives for future Excadrill matchups.

decisions.rationale: Charizard leads to threaten Whimsicott with Fire Blast before Tailwind sets up, and can Mega-Y for Drought. Rotom-Wash pivots with Volt Switch, pressures Tauros with Water STAB, and Levitate gives Ground immunity. Toxapex back provides Regenerator physical walling for Tauros/CloseCombat and Toxic Spikes. Venusaur back gives special bulk, Chlorophyll + Drought synergy, and Giga Drain/Sludge Bomb coverage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent dual-weather: Whimsicott Focus Sash Tailwind + Charizard-Mega-Y Drought core, Ninetales-Alola Snowscape backup. Tauros-Paldea-Blaze is primary wincon; Blastoise-Mega mid-game special wall. Gholdengo and Maushold are surprise bench picks. Need dedicated Ice/Fighting answers; Rotom-Wash slot may need replacement with dedicated Tauros/Ninetales answer in future games. Preserve Charizard for favorable matchups; avoid leading into Snowscape.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind guarantees speed control before either foe acts, letting Tauros reliably pressure both targets. Rock Slide is spread and 4x super effective into Charizard, with a possible OHKO even through spread reduction; it also chips Rotom. This preserves offensive pressure while avoiding a risky switch.

decisions.rationale: Fire Blast pressures Whimsicott at 2x with Focus Sash guaranteeing it stays to Tailwind or Encore next turn. Hydro Pump pressures Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (primary wincon) at 2x. Skipping Mega preserves Charizard's Speed at 165 and hides Mega timing for a more favorable turn.

Preserve Charizard Mega for mid-game when speed matchup is clearer. Rotom-Wash may need replacement vs dedicated Ice/Fighting answers later. Avoid leading into Snowscape matchups.

decisions.rationale: Switch Toxapex into Whimsicott; Regenerator and Bold bulk let it absorb Moonblast while SludgeBomb hits Fairy SE. Rotom-Wash stays to pressure with Hydro Pump. Avoid leading with Venusaur into uncertain matchups.
decisions.notebook: Tauros-Paldea-Blaze is gone; Charizard fainted turn 1. Opponent likely Whimsicott + one of Ninetales-Alola/Blastoise/Gholdengo/Maushold. Preserve Mega Charizard-Y for mid-game when speed dynamics are clearer. Toxapex pivots into Fairy/Grass cores. Rotom-Wash may need future replacement vs Ice/Fighting answers. Avoid Snowscape matchups.

selection: Aurora Veil (your side, including ally Whimsicott)
decisions.rationale: Encore Rotom-Wash to punish or force out its revealed Hydro Pump while Whimsicott acts first under Tailwind. Ninetales sets Aurora Veil in the active snow, improving both Pokémon’s durability against the remaining revealed threats and preserving offensive options next turn.

decisions.rationale: Encore Toxapex before it can act locks its previously used Toxic Spikes, preventing meaningful progress. Gholdengo then removes the weakened Venusaur with Shadow Ball before Venusaur’s possible move; this preserves pressure while avoiding a risky spread attack.

Toxapex Recovers to full HP to absorb Gholdengo's spread hit and stay healthy for the next turn. Venusaur uses Sludge Bomb on Whimsicott (4x super-effective) to KO the badly poisoned Prankster threat, removing Helping Hand support for Gholdengo. Even if Venusaur takes a hit from boosted Make It Rain, it likely survives to fire.

Next priority: handle Gholdengo with Toxapex bulk + Rotom-Wash pivoting. Venusaur must stay alive past Ninetales-Alola's Blizzard threat (now neutralized).

Toxapex is Encore-locked into Toxic Spikes (forced). Rotom-Wash Protects to avoid Gholdengo's potential Helping Hand-boosted Make It Rain spread, which threatens significant damage. Protect also lets bad poison tick on Whimsicott, nudging it closer to KO range next turn while preserving Rotom-Wash's HP.

reflections.summary: Won because the opening Rock Slide immediately removed Mega Charizard-Y, while Tailwind and repeated Encore punished the opponent’s Protect/Toxic Spikes pattern. Gholdengo then safely cleaned up Venusaur, Toxapex, and Rotom. The four brought were effective overall; no Mega evolution was used, which suited this sun matchup better than relying on Mega Blastoise.
reflections.adjustment: Expect Excadrill or Weavile next: consider replacing Tauros with Maushold while retaining Whimsicott, Ninetales, and Gholdengo. Preserve Gholdengo rather than trading it early, and avoid committing to Mega Blastoise in the opponent’s sun.
reflections.notebook: Opponent repeatedly used Protect with Rotom and Toxapex while prioritizing Toxic Spikes; Encore plus speed control is effective against this pattern. Mega Charizard-Y/Venusaur remains a central sun mode, but the opponent may rotate in confirmed Focus Sash Mold Breaker Excadrill or Life Orb Weavile next game. Keep Gholdengo as a preferred Excadrill matchup option and consider Maushold as the fourth slot; do not rely on Mega Blastoise into sun. Tauros can pressure Charizard with Rock Slide but is vulnerable to Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump, so avoid treating it as a durable lead.

reflections.summary: Lost because Gholdengo + Whimsicott formed an unanswerable defensive-offensive core that dismantled the team piece by piece. Mega Charizard-Y fainted turn 1 to Tauros Rock Slide without ever attacking, Venusaur and Toxapex were each killed by Gholdengo's Shadow Ball, and Rotom-Wash was double-teamed (Whimsicott Moonblast + Gholdengo Shadow Ball) after being locked into Protect by Encore. The team had no way to threaten Gholdengo (both Water STABs resisted), and Toxapex's Toxic Spikes repeatedly failed to stick. Mega Charizard-Y's Drought sweep never materialized.
reflections.adjustment: Re-evaluate the team preview slot held by Mega Charizard-Y: it must either Mega Evolve and attack immediately on the turn it switches in, or it is dead weight against faster leads. Consider replacing it or its item with a Pokemon that threatens Steel/Ghost types (e.g., a Fighting or Ground attacker), or at minimum ensure the Mega Evolution is triggered on turn 1 via a teammate's speed control rather than leading with it into a Rock Slide. Also, do not double-slot for Water STAB when the opponent's core resists both.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Gholdengo: Leftovers, Shadow Ball/Recover/MakeItRain/Protect, Timid — extremely self-sufficient bulky attacker; immune to Helping Hand by Steel typing (deliberate Whimsicott pairing synergy). Opponent Whimsicott: Focus Sash, Prankster Encore/Tailwind/Moonblast/Helping Hand — shuts down pivoting and recovery; prioritize eliminating before it Encore-locks your win condition. Toxic Spikes failed to stick multiple times — opponent's switches and move choices prevented layering. Both our Water STABs (Hydro Pump, Liquidation) are resisted by Gholdengo and Whimsicott — avoid double-slotting Water coverage against this archetype. Aurora Veil Ninetales-Alola Blizzard is a Venusaur threat even through Protect. Opponent did not bring Blastoise or Maushold — their full roster was built around the Whimsicott/Gholdengo core. Future plan: ensure Mega Charizard-Y activates and attacks on the turn it enters, or replace with a Steel/Ghost/threatening answer to Gholdengo.
